newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto weighs options for chemical units.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto weighs options for chemical units.

text.p: Monsanto Co said Thursday it is analyzying alternatives for the future of its chemical businesses.
Monsanto said it is considering several possibilities, including separating the corporation into two public companies -- one a life sciences company and the other a chemical company.

Another alternative includes combining the chemical businesses with one or more companies. A spokeswoman said that option would include the possible merger of its chemical businesses into companies outside of Monsanto.
Or, Monsanto said it could opt to keep the chemical businesses and restructure them.

"In recent years, the strategies and needs of the chemical and life sciences businesses have become quite different," Robert Shapiro, Monsanto chairman, said in a statement. "It's in the best interest of our people, our customers and our shareowners that we take appropriate steps to allow all of our businesses to reach their maximum potential."
He added that Monsanto will move as fast as it can to make a decision. "...(B)ut we'll take the time needed to make the right decisions."
Monsanto's chemical businesses include nylon fibers, specialty chemicals and Saflex, a plastic interlayer sold to glass manufacturers.
